title: A Residence at Nagasaki and Hakodate in 1859–1860
subtitle: With an Account of Japan Generally. With a Series of Letters on Japan, by His Wife
short_title: A Residence at Nagasaki and Hakodate

source.contributor: Royal Asiatic Society, Bombay (Digital Library of India)

summary: C. Pemberton Hodgson (1821–1865) was the first British consul at Nagasaki, from June 1859, and then consul at Hakodate in the north of Japan until 1860. He describes his meetings with the governor of Nagasaki and other officials, the money system, the voyage from Nagasaki to Yedo and Hakodate, and four excursions into the country around Hakodate, written as letters to Rutherford Alcock, the British minister. A chapter of letters from his wife to her mother tells of the voyage to Nagasaki and of their life there. The later chapters are on Japanese priests, government, princes and daimios, governors, doctors, houses, and money, with cuts of the coins, on the importance of Hakodate and the Russian settlements to the north, and on natural history. The book ends with a catalogue of Japanese plants sent by Sir William Hooker of Kew.
